description: Declarative surface of the human review layer. 'sections' is the closed set of sections both review.json and decisions.json may carry, in the order a reader meets them; a decisions file naming anything else is rejected whole. 'drop_cap_decisions' is the closed vocabulary of the drop_caps section's values, declared here so the validator refuses an unknown verdict from the batch the section is introduced in rather than from the batch that first consumes it. 'review_format_version' stamps every exported draft, so a draft written by an older layer is recognisable rather than silently reinterpreted. 'translator_view_chars' bounds the excerpt of the text the translator was actually offered that the terms section carries beside the joined rendering a human is shown; the two differ wherever a paragraph is set in several styles, and a ruling written from the rendering cannot match the offered text, so the excerpt is what makes that disagreement visible at review time. 'matched_prompt_excerpts' bounds how many offered texts an applied ruling records per term as evidence of what it reached; the count itself is always recorded whole. Version 2 of the draft merges the two finders into one terms table and derives what a personal name defaults to from the run's declared name policy, so a row carries auto_target as the default the run will land under, observed_target as what a model said, candidates as the other forms the policy offers, and person_shaped as whether the derivation applied to it at all. A version 1 draft and a version 1 decisions file still parse: a ruling is a mapping of source to target in either version, and nothing about consuming one reads the version.
